reports.category: Report Miscellaneous Crypto Scams with Chainabuse: Purchase of fake vehicle via Coin Base with Bitcoin
reports.description:
I was scammed by someone pretending to be selling their vehicle via ebay. I was sent an invoice and spoke to a fake customer service representative who walked me through the process. I have now lost $17,000. I realize this is not ebays fault nor did Bitcoin have anything to do with it, but something needs to be done to be sure this does not happen to anyone ever again.  
_x000D_
The fake seller went by the name Toth Nicole. I have several email messages from the address tothnicole@comcast.net._x000D_
_x000D_
The phone number on the invoice is no longer active, but that is the number I used on Tuesday Nov. 10, 2020 to complete the transaction via Coinbase. The fake ebay rep had me change my currency to Bitcoin and then sent me a code to post in the recipient box. When I did not receive confirmation or delivery info I investigated and determined I was victim of a scam._x000D_
_x000D_
Anything you can do to help apprehend this person would be greatly appreciated. Im a school teacher, and $17,000 is a lot of money to me._x000D_
_x000D_
Catherine G.

reports.category: Report Miscellaneous Crypto Scams with Chainabuse: Investment scam
reports.description:
In July 2020, I came upon an employee of RealFXProTrades named Joe Alexander on Facebook. The client claims to have seen a post from Joe Alexander saying that they would be showing how to make money through cryptocurrencies and to ‚Äúsend a PM‚Äù if interested. I sent a Whatsapp message to Joe Alexander, wherein he replied by asking her how much of an initial deposit she could make. I began by making her first deposit, and was shown to be making profits after a few days. After a few more days had passed, my profits had grown immensely.  
At this point, I decided that I wanted to withdraw. When I put in the request, I was told that I had to pay fees, and every time I paid, she received additional demands for other fees. This continued on for about a year and a half. I was even told to pay a delay fee because of how long the process had been going on. _x000D_
Throughout all this, I was told that this is a legitimate practice and that the website was a trustworthy platform, and was promised that I would get her profits in the end. _x000D_
At a certain point, I decided that I had enough, and went to the police to report on me case, but was told that I required more evidence to report the scammer.

Ancient password hack, probably obtained through a security breach on a website. Threatens to release naughty pictures to my contacts unless I send $723 USD to this BTC wallet: 1LuiqwsE5HF9T2mkS8EN3TLkJRFdbzrR8k. Claims to have malware within my security domain. Same as all the others. 
Use a password manager like KeePass, dont save any passwords on any of your devices. Make a complex password UNIQUE FOR EVERY SITE, and store it in your password manager. Youll need one master passPHRASE (complex) in the password manager app that you will need to remember, so the password manager app can fill in the appropriate one for the website. That will give let you know which website got breached. Change passwords regularly and store them in the password manager, keep track of what the old password was, the site, and the date you changed it. Then you can complain to the websites security administration. Keep it in a secured folder or air-gapped in a thumb drive in a SAFE PLACE if you do this.
